summary: Radar for 3 Nov 2026, GLP-1 focus. Nothing in this batch is fresh randomized head-to-head data, so no news item qualifies for an extra L2 long-form. Lilly's "Zepbound 4.5% more weight loss than Wegovy HD" (29 Oct) is an indirect comparison across separate trials, not a head-to-head. It suits a 13:00 Short only, worded as "separate trials, not head-to-head". The best long-form opportunities are still the Lane A topics in the playbook. (1) Stopping tirzepatide: demand is still climbing (momentum 82→87 across our snapshots), with fresh mainstream pickup in Daily Maverick (2 Nov) and the Metabolites regain review. (2) Fatigue. (3) Birth control, now with a new pregnancy-exposure meta-analysis (Front Pharmacol, 16 Oct). (4) Injection site reactions, with a new semaglutide skin-reaction meta-analysis of RCTs. (5) Dehydration. Thanksgiving is building toward its 18–27 Nov peak and should feed the live long-form through 20:00 funnel Shorts. New, early Short hooks: (a) bones: Medscape's "GLP-1s not linked to more fractures in three studies" (2 Nov), plus a Bone meta-analysis of placebo-controlled RCTs (2 Nov), mostly older GLP-1 medicines; our bones Short got 242 views. (b) Food noise: a Penn State survey (2 Nov) reports frequent food noise in about 1 in 5 people. It was higher in current GLP-1 users, but the survey is cross-sectional, so it needs careful framing. It funnels to the Food Noise long-form. (c) Alcohol: Harvard Gazette (2 Nov) reports that about half of drinkers on GLP-1s drank less, which builds on our earlier alcohol snapshots. (d) Menopause hormone therapy and response to GLP-1s: observational, and that cohort has underperformed for us before. Watch items: a reported TGA approval of the Wegovy pill in Australia (500+ Google Trends searches in AU; several AU outlets on 3 Nov, but our search results were mixed, so check the TGA's register (ARTG) before publishing). ObesityWeek runs 14–17 Nov (full REDEFINE 4 results expected). Retatrutide gray-market seizures plus a Cureus case report of liver injury from an unregulated product sold as retatrutide: at most 1 gray-market Short this week, with the not-approved line. Rejected: buy-online, research-peptide and promo-code pieces (Forbes, Costa Rica retatrutide, HealSend, Protocol MD). Employer-coverage and cost news is banned for the channel.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (783 began the lead-in; 335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88 on placebo) plus the Metabolites systematic review of regain after GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 medicines (Oct 9)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 14:00. Open with the literal answer: in SURMOUNT-4, people switched to placebo regained part of their weight, while people who stayed on tirzepatide kept losing. Then a 'you' scenario: thinking about a break. Explain why appetite returns: GLP-1 and GIP signalling stops; it isn't a willpower failure. Cover what the review says about habits that help, and when to talk to your prescriber. Say 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'. Link to How Long and Protein. Check the speech-to-text transcript against the script for every number.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: Steady now; second bump in early January (New Year 'should I stop?' searches)
candidates.why_now: Momentum has climbed across 5 snapshots (82→87). New mainstream pickup: Daily Maverick 'Life after weight-loss medication: what happens when the injections stop?' (Nov 2). The Metabolites review is still recent. Our first attempt dropped in production, so this slot is unfilled and the cluster needs it.

candidates.topic: Why am I so tired on tirzepatide? The Zepbound label lists fatigue in 5% (5 mg), 6% (10 mg) and 7% (15 mg) vs 3% on placebo
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. First line: some tiredness is a listed, usually mild side effect, reported more often than on placebo. Then the likely everyday contributors: eating much less, low protein, fluids, sleep. Give practical habits, and when to call your prescriber (dizziness, signs of dehydration, low blood sugar if also on insulin or a sulfonylurea). Keep 'linked to' wording and avoid 'that's why' claims.

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide weaken your bones? Medscape: 'GLP-1 therapies not linked to increased fracture risk in three studies' (Nov 2) plus a new Bone meta-analysis of placebo-controlled RCTs on bone metabolism (Nov 2)
candidates.angle: 08:00 body-worry reassurance Short: 'Will tirzepatide weaken my bones?' Honest answer: in these studies of GLP-1 medicines (mostly older GLP-1 drugs and observational designs), more fractures weren't seen. Fast weight loss can still affect bone, so strength training, protein and enough calcium and vitamin D matter. Say 'GLP-1 medicines' for class data, and point to the live Bones & Muscle long-form.
candidates.why_now: Two independent new sources in 24 h (Medscape roundup and the Bone meta-analysis). Few creators have covered it yet. Our bones Short is our second-best reassurance Short (242), and the Bones & Muscle long-form can absorb the clicks.
